brief: Four panels comparing data matching modes: Longest List (repeats last), Shortest List (truncates), Cross Reference (all combinations), Longest List with graft
context: Title: 'Data Matching'. Four purple-backgrounded panels showing the same operation with different matching rules. Top-left: Longest List â€” when lists have different lengths, the shorter list's last item is repeated. Top-middle: Shortest List â€” truncates to the shorter list's length. Top-right: Cross Reference â€” creates all possible combinations (Cartesian product). Panel shows many more results. Bottom-left: Longest List with data grafting applied â€” changes the tree structure. Each panel shows Param Viewer with data tree structure and a Panel with the resulting values. Rhino viewport screenshots (pink borders) show the geometric results of each matching mode.
category: Beginner - Curves Tangents and Data Trees
solution_principle: Data matching controls how Grasshopper pairs items from lists of different lengths. Longest List (default): repeats the last item of shorter lists. Shortest List: stops at the shorter list's end â€” no repetition. Cross Reference: every item paired with every other item â€” Cartesian product. Right-click a component input to change matching mode. Understanding this is critical for controlling output quantity.
